title: Evaluation of Patients Receiving Intravitreal Anti-VEGF for Diabetic Macular Edema in Clinical Practice in the United States
database_or_data_source: Vestrum Health treatment and outcomes database; deidentified EMRs queried by SQL
study_period: Index first anti-VEGF injection from 2012-01-01 to 2015-04-30; observation through 2017-04-30
practice_or_database_size: 251 retina specialists at 54 private US clinics; records include demographics, procedures, diagnoses, medications, and outcomes including VA
dme_definition: Eyes newly diagnosed with DME in the Vestrum database and administered a first anti-VEGF injection
treatment_naive_definition: No prior anti-VEGF treatment recorded before first anti-VEGF injection in the study window; outside-practice prior treatment cannot be fully ruled out from extracted text
sample_screened_or_assessed: 155,240 DME eyes assessed; 13,016 with first anti-VEGF treatment and VA on index
sample_included: Year-1 cohort 3,028 eyes; year-2 cohort 1,292 eyes
follow_up_window: 12 and 24 months after index injection; month-12 VA closest to 12 months in months 11-12; required VA at index, month 12, and at least once each quarter
key_inclusion_exclusion: Included newly diagnosed DME eyes receiving first anti-VEGF injection and accepted VA methods. Excluded treatment break greater than 11 months in 24 months after index and eyes not meeting VA/follow-up requirements; required same VA methodology per patient.
confounding_exclusions: Focused on newly diagnosed DME and anti-VEGF treated eyes; extracted text does not show detailed exclusion of other retinal diagnoses comparable to later papers
treatment_or_exposure_groups: Injection intensity groups: <=6 versus >6 injections per year; year-2 maintained or reduced frequency subgroups
va_method: Converted to ETDRS letters with ETDRS = 85 - (50 * logMAR)
outcome_domains: VA change and anti-VEGF injection frequency/intensity over 1 and 2 years
statistical_methods: Descriptive statistics; paired t-tests within cohorts; independent t-tests assuming unequal variance between cohorts; p < 0.05; Excel
key_results_for_method_context: Higher injection intensity in year 1 produced greater VA gain (+8.0 letters with >6 injections vs +3.7 with <=6). Reducing frequency after high year-1 dosing was associated with greater year-2 loss.
attrition_selection: Strict VA/follow-up requirements reduced 13,016 potentially eligible index-treatment eyes to 3,028 year-1 eyes and 1,292 year-2 eyes.
limitations_or_caveats: Strict follow-up/VA requirements select for more observed patients; retrospective EMR design and treatment-selection confounding.
methods_relevance: Strong template for treatment-intensity analyses with index injection, prespecified VA windows, quarterly VA, and injection-frequency cohorts.

treatment_or_exposure_groups: Untreated, anti-VEGF monotherapy, steroid monotherapy, focal laser monotherapy, and combination treatment patterns by year and cumulatively
